subject: Music Production
title: The Fairlight CMI Revolution
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Fairlight CMI Revolution usable.

hook.text: In 1979, the Fairlight CMI became the first commercial digital sampler, costing over twenty-five thousand dollars.

buildup.text: It could record any real-world sound and play it back from a keyboard at different pitches.

discovery.text: Peter Gabriel and Kate Bush were among the first artists to feature the Fairlight on hit records.

twist.text: Its signature orchestra hit sample appeared in so many 1980s songs that it became a running joke.

climax.text: The Fairlight proved that sampling could be a mainstream production tool, not just an experiment.

punchline.text: One pricey machine made sampling a pop music tool.

quiz.question: What was notable about the Fairlight CMI?
options: It was the first electric guitar
It was the first commercial digital sampler
It was the cheapest synthesizer available
